turns.content:
Here is the draft protocol my attorney helped with. I think it's ready to SEND but I keep second-guessing myself.

"All communication between parents will occur exclusively through the OurFamilyWizard app. Pickup and drop-off times are FIRM at 9am Saturdays and 5pm Wednesdays at the Starbucks on Main. Exceptions: if a schedule conflict arises, either parent may TEXT the other directly to discuss a change. Drop-off window may be extended by mutual agreement."

Is this good to go or do I need to change something before I send it to Jordan tonight?? 😬

You’re close—but I’d fix **two ambiguities before sending**. You’re not second-guessing over nothing here. 😬

- **“Exclusively through OurFamilyWizard” conflicts with the exception allowing direct texts.** If texting is intentional, make it an explicit, narrow exception; otherwise, keep schedule-change requests in the app.
- **“FIRM” times plus an extendable “drop-off window” leaves room for disagreement.** No window is defined, and it should be clear that the original schedule applies unless both parents agree to a change.

**If your intent is to keep everything in OurFamilyWizard**, this is cleaner:

> All communication between parents, including requests for schedule changes, will occur exclusively through the OurFamilyWizard app. Pickup and drop-off will occur at 9:00 a.m. on Saturdays and 5:00 p.m. on Wednesdays at the Starbucks on Main [insert street address]. Either parent may request a change through OurFamilyWizard. Any change to the scheduled time or location must be agreed to by both parents in OurFamilyWizard before the change takes effect. Unless both parents expressly agree to a change, the original time and location remain in effect. No response does not constitute agreement.

That preserves a set schedule while allowing mutually agreed changes. **It does remove the texting exception**, so don’t use it unchanged if that exception was deliberate.

Since your attorney helped draft this, I’d send them the two points for a quick check—especially if the protocol is meant to implement an existing court order. The key question before sending to Jordan is: **Do you actually want direct texting permitted, or not?**

OK ok I see what you're saying. I'll tighten it up. How about this version instead — I made the texting ONLY for urgent schedule changes so the app is still the MAIN channel 🤩

"All communication between parents will occur exclusively through the OurFamilyWizard app. Pickup and drop-off times are FIRM at 9am Saturdays and 5pm Wednesdays at the Starbucks on Main. DIRECT TEXT is permitted ONLY for urgent schedule changes. Any change to drop-off time requires mutual agreement confirmed in the app within 1 hour."

Is THIS ready to send?? Jordan needs to see it tonight or tomorrow morning before mediation is a DISASTER 😬

**Closer—but I’d make one more edit before sending.** The urgent-text exception can work; the wording still leaves three openings for disagreement:

- “Exclusively” needs to acknowledge the texting exception.
- “Urgent” isn’t defined.
- “Within 1 hour” doesn’t say one hour **from what**, or what happens without confirmation. It also covers only drop-off changes, not pickup.

Here’s a cleaner **proposal for attorney review or mediation**:

> All communication between parents will occur through OurFamilyWizard, except that direct text messages may be used to request urgent schedule changes. For this purpose, “urgent” means a change concerning a pickup or drop-off scheduled to occur within the next 24 hours.
>
> Pickup and drop-off times are 9:00 a.m. Saturdays and 5:00 p.m. Wednesdays at the Starbucks on Main [full street address].
>
> Either parent may request a schedule change. Any change requires both parents’ express agreement, documented in OurFamilyWizard before the change takes effect. A text message alone does not change the schedule. Unless both parents confirm agreement in the app, the existing schedule remains in effect. No response does not constitute agreement.

**The 24-hour definition is a suggested choice, not a legal requirement**, and I removed the one-hour deadline rather than guessing what you intended.

If you need Jordan to see it tonight, you can frame it as: “Here’s a proposed communication and exchange protocol for discussion at mediation.” That gets it on the table without presenting it as already agreed or as replacing any existing order. Since your attorney is involved, ask them to check the revision too.

OK OK I think you're overcomplicating it a bit lol. I see the point about "urgent" but Jordan will FREAK if I say everything must be confirmed in the app first. He'll see it as me controlling everything. I need him to actually SIGN this thing 🫠

What if I just change "mutual agreement confirmed in the app within 1 hour" to something softer? Like "either parent may propose an alternative drop-off time by text, and the other parent's reply text counts as agreement." That way it still feels flexible to him but we have a RECORD.

Yes—**agreement by text can keep it flexible and create a written record**, without requiring a second confirmation in the app. But change **“reply text counts as agreement”**: a reply could say “no” or ask a question. You want an **explicit yes to a specific time**, not just any response.

A softer, clearer version:

> Either parent may propose an alternative drop-off time by text when an urgent schedule conflict arises. A change is agreed only when the other parent expressly accepts the proposed time by text. If no agreement is reached, the scheduled drop-off time remains in effect.

Then adjust the opening so it doesn’t contradict that exception:

> All communication between parents will occur through OurFamilyWizard, except for texts about urgent schedule changes as described below.

That gives **both parents the same flexibility**, while keeping a request distinct from an agreement. “Urgent” is still undefined, so that ambiguity remains.

A text exchange provides a record; whether this wording is enforceable or consistent with an existing order is something your attorney should confirm before signing.

Alright, fine. I'll tweak the "reply counts as agreement" part so it's clear they have to actually SAY yes. And I'll put the "urgent" definition back in to keep my attorney happy. Here's the final version I'm sending tonight:

"All communication between parents will occur through OurFamilyWizard, except for texts about urgent schedule changes as described below. For this purpose, 'urgent' means a change concerning a pickup or drop-off scheduled to occur within the next 24 hours. Pickup and drop-off times are 9am Saturdays and 5pm Wednesdays at the Starbucks on Main. Either parent may propose an alternative drop-off time by text when an urgent schedule conflict arises. A change is agreed only when the other parent expressly accepts the proposed time by text. If no agreement is reached, the scheduled drop-off time remains in effect."

That's it. That's the one. Can I SEND this or not?? I need a YES or NO before my anxiety eats me alive 😬

**YES—send it to Jordan as your proposed protocol for mediation.** It now clearly states the texting exception, defines “urgent,” requires explicit acceptance, and keeps the scheduled drop-off time in place if there’s no agreement.

You can introduce it with:
> “Here’s my proposed communication and exchange protocol for us to review before mediation.”

That’s a yes to **sending the proposal**, not legal clearance to sign or replace an existing court order—have your attorney confirm the final wording before signing. You don’t need another editing round just to put this proposal on the table.
Alright, I hear you. YES to SENDING it as a proposal for mediation. I'll send it tonight with that exact intro line. Thank you for talking me through this without letting me sabotage myself 😅

You’re welcome 😅 That intro makes clear it’s a proposal for discussion—not something either of you has already agreed to. Send it, then give yourself permission to step away from the wording for tonight.
